Patch both files (their current texts follow) and return each WHOLE; change nothing else in them. types.ts: BuildInput gains the optional field `hide?: Record<string, string[]>` after vendor. buildAcceptances.ts: a member whose customId is an OWN key of input.hide gets ctx.siblings = its siblings followed by each path of input.hide[customId] the list does not hold yet, and ctx.fullExclude = checks.fullExclude followed by each such path it does not hold yet (new arrays; checks is never changed); every other check, message, order and field stays exactly as it is. Write no test file: a probe tests you and a judge writes the example tests.

## Function Build Acceptances

Sets the acceptance of every card the checks name, from its generation's siblings and the texts read.

Behaviour: buildAcceptances({cards, checks, profile, texts}). A profile other than typescript and go → {ok: false, errors: ["no acceptance builder for language '<id>' (only typescript, go)"]}. Else the errors, in this order: the guard, then the locator, holding any of the six heredoc tags (HEREDOC_TAGS: MORPH_GUARD_EOF, MORPH_CONF_EOF, MORPH_TSCONF_EOF, MORPH_FIRSTDIFF_EOF, MORPH_PROBE_EOF, MORPH_LITS_EOF) → "the guard holds the heredoc tag <tag>" / "the first-difference locator holds …", one per tag; then per checks card in order: no card of that id → "checks card '<id>' is not in the deck" (nothing more on it); no target with an extension of the profile → "card '<id>' has no <profile id> target" (a wrong profile is refused, never built); a judge (files not null) whose file paths are not exactly its targets → "judge '<id>': files <JSON of the paths> are not its targets <JSON of the targets>"; a code card without texts.probes[id] → "code card '<id>' has no probe", a probe holding a tag → "the probe of <id> holds the heredoc tag <tag>"; smoke null with a test target → "code card '<id>' targets the test <test> but has no smoke cap"; smoke with no test target → "code card '<id>' has a smoke cap but no test target". Any error → {ok: false, errors}. The members are the named cards in the checks' order; their generations are Layer Generations of the members alone (a dependency outside them is ignored); a member's siblings are the targets of the other members of its generation, in the checks' order. Each member gets Code Acceptance or Judge Acceptance — with the go profile builder-go's goCodeAcceptance or goJudgeAcceptance, same arguments — with ctx {id, phase, targets, siblings, frozen, fullExclude, ownGit, profile, guard, firstdiff, allowed, vendor} — P19: the input's optional uses (Plan Spec's, customId → declared names) and vendor (vendor/modules.txt exists), absent {} and false; allowed = uses[customId] as given when uses has that own key, else []; vendor = input.vendor === true; nothing else reads them. → {ok: true, cards}: the input cards in their order, each member a copy with its acceptance, every other card as given. probeFile(profile, id) (exported; cli reads the probe by it) = "_<id>_probe_test.go" for the go profile (the leading "_" makes the go tool ignore the file where it is kept, decks/<phase>/parts), else "<id>.probe.ts". P21 (#12): the input's optional hide (customId → paths; Plan Command's Hide Later for a Go --only cut) appends hide[customId] (an own key) to a member's ctx siblings and to its ctx fullExclude, each path a list already holds skipped; no hide or no key → as before.

Steps:
- calls: Code Acceptance
- calls: Judge Acceptance
- reads: Checks
- uses: cards
- uses: builder-go
- produces: Build Result

1. given the P10a deck file decks/p10/v2deck.json (12 cards) with every acceptance set to null; checks p10.checks.typed.json; the typescript profile; texts guard.p10.txt, firstdiff.p10.txt and probes {<id>: decks/p10/parts/<id>.probe.ts} for the six code cards; when buildAcceptances; then {ok: true, cards} equal to the cards of decks/p10/v2deck.json — the 12 acceptances byte for byte as build.py p10 wrote them (the golden check) (ref: tests/fixtures/builder/guard.p10.txt, tests/fixtures/builder/firstdiff.p10.txt, tests/fixtures/builder/p10.checks.typed.json)

3. given cards a (["src/x/a.ts", "tests/x/a.test.ts"]), j (["tests/x/j.examples.test.ts"]); checks cards a, j (files [tests/x/k.examples.test.ts]), z; probes {}; guard "x MORPH_PROBE_EOF"; when buildAcceptances; then {ok: false, errors: ["the guard holds the heredoc tag MORPH_PROBE_EOF", "code card 'a' has no probe", "code card 'a' targets the test tests/x/a.test.ts but has no smoke cap", "judge 'j': files [\"tests/x/k.examples.test.ts\"] are not its targets [\"tests/x/j.examples.test.ts\"]", "checks card 'z' is not in the deck"]}
4. given any input with the python profile; when buildAcceptances; then {ok: false, errors: ["no acceptance builder for language 'python' (only typescript, go)"]}
5. given the go profile; cards percent-of (["calc/percent_of.go"]) and clamp-value-judge (["calc/clamp_value_examples_test.go"]), one generation, acceptances null; checks phase "m1", frozen ["go.mod", "internal"], cards percent-of and clamp-value-judge (files [{calc/clamp_value_examples_test.go, min 4, max 10, lits ["TestClampValueExample1"], new true}]); probes {percent-of: "package calc\n"}; guard "// guard\n", firstdiff "// firstdiff\n"; when buildAcceptances; then ok; percent-of's acceptance = code1.txt (goCodeAcceptance, siblings ["calc/clamp_value_examples_test.go"]); the judge's = goJudgeAcceptance with siblings ["calc/percent_of.go"] (ref: tests/fixtures/builder/go/code1.txt (percent-of's whole script))

7. given cards a (["src/x/a.ts"]), b (["src/x/b.ts"]), acceptances null; checks phase "p7" with cards a, b; probes a, b "// probe\n"; guard "// guard\n", firstdiff "// firstdiff\n"; uses {"a": ["zod", "yaml"], "a-judge": ["ajv"], "c": ["x"]}, vendor true; then the same input without uses and vendor; when buildAcceptances; then ok; a's acceptance = codeAcceptance(ctx {id "a", phase "p7", targets ["src/x/a.ts"], siblings ["src/x/b.ts"], frozen DEFAULT_FROZEN, fullExclude [], ownGit false, typescript, the texts, allowed ["zod", "yaml"]}, "// probe\n", null, null), holding "node $P/guard.mjs src src/x/a.ts 'zod,yaml'\n"; b's = codeAcceptance with siblings ["src/x/a.ts"], holding "node $P/guard.mjs src src/x/b.ts\n"; then a's holds "node $P/guard.mjs src src/x/a.ts\n" and b's is the same as before
8. given the go input of example 5 plus uses {"percent-of": ["github.com/dustin/go-humanize", "golang.org/x/text"]} and vendor true; when buildAcceptances; then ok; percent-of's acceptance = code1.txt with "export GOFLAGS=-mod=mod " become "export GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor " and its guard line "node $P/guard.mjs src calc/percent_of.go" ending in " 'github.com/dustin/go-humanize,golang.org/x/text'"; the judge's = goJudgeAcceptance(its ctx with siblings ["calc/percent_of.go"] and vendor true, files), holding "export GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor " and no "-mod=mod" (ref: tests/fixtures/builder/go/code1.txt)
9. given examples.json["Build Acceptances 9"].given; when buildAcceptances; then examples.json["Build Acceptances 9"].then (ref: tests/fixtures/builder/examples.json)

Data Checks: A phase's acceptance knobs, read from its checks document (decks/<phase>/checks.json).
Schema:
{ version: 1, phase: string, parts: string, frozen: string[], fullExclude: string[], ownGit: boolean, cards: { id: string, smoke: number | null, extra: string | null, files: JudgeFile[] | null }[] }

Data Build Result: The cards with their acceptances, or every error.
Schema:
{ ok: true, cards: Card[] } | { ok: false, errors: string[] }

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

## Function Hide Later

The Go files of an --only subset each card hides because the run has not written them yet.

Behaviour: hideLater(plan, tree), tree = Go Tree. plan.generations shorter than 2 → {} (a one-generation subset keeps P20's acceptances byte for byte). Else for every card c of plan.cards, with g the index of the generation holding c's customId: hide = the targets ending ".go" of every OTHER card of plan.cards whose generation index is >= g (its siblings and every later card), in plan.cards order and then target order, each once. Then, until no directory qualifies: a directory D (path.posix.dirname) of a file in hide qualifies when the non-test files of D in tree.files (dirname D, not ending "_test.go") are at least one and all in hide, and a file of tree.files NOT in hide lies in D or imports D (tree.imports[file] holds D) — a package hidden whole that a visible file still uses; those non-test files are removed from hide (D's test files stay hidden). → {<c.customId>: hide} for every card of plan.cards, an empty list included. The plan and the tree are never changed. A card's own package is never hidden whole: its own target is never in its hide.

Steps:
- reads: Plan
- reads: Go Tree
- produces: Hide Map

2. given hide.plan.json; hide.tree.json plus "cmd/tool/main.go" (files sorted again) importing ["summary"]; when hideLater; then {"s": ["calc/ratio_of.go", "calc/scale_value_examples_test.go", "report/format_line_examples_test.go", "summary/summary_examples_test.go"], "f": ["calc/ratio_of.go", "calc/scale_value_examples_test.go", "report/format_line_examples_test.go", "summary/summary_examples_test.go"], "r": ["calc/scale_value_examples_test.go", "report/format_line_examples_test.go", "summary/summary_examples_test.go"], "sj": ["calc/ratio_of.go", "report/format_line_examples_test.go", "summary/summary_examples_test.go"], "fj": ["summary/summary_examples_test.go"], "m": ["report/format_line_examples_test.go", "summary/summary_examples_test.go"], "mj": []} — summary.go is kept for main.go, then format_line.go for summary.go
3. given hide.plan.json; hide.tree.json plus "summary/legacy_test.go" (files sorted again) importing []; when hideLater; then the result of example 2 — a kept test file in summary/ keeps summary.go, then format_line.go
4. given hide.plan.json with cards [its s] and generations [["s"]]; then hide.plan.json and hide.tree.json without "summary/summary.go" (the file and its imports key) plus "cmd/tool/main.go" importing ["summary"]; when hideLater; then {}; then the result of example 1 — summary/ has no non-test file on disk, so nothing qualifies

Data Plan: The result of planSpec and the body of the plan document.
Schema:
{ spec: string, components: string[], cards: Card[], generations: string[][], externalDependsOn: Record<string, string[]> }

Data Go Tree: The Go files of a module (relative, sorted) and, per file, the module's own packages it imports as directories.
Schema:
{ files: string[]; imports: Record<string, string[]> }

Data Hide Map: Per card of a subset, the Go files its acceptance hides beyond its generation's siblings.
Schema:
Record<string, string[]>

## Function Read Go Tree

The Go files of a module and the module's own packages each imports.

Behaviour: readGoTree(root). The module path is the first line of root/go.mod matching `module <path>` (no go.mod, or no such line → none). files: every regular file whose name ends ".go" under root, walking directories (a symbolic link is not followed) and skipping every directory named "vendor" or "testdata" or whose name starts with "." or "_", and every file whose name starts with "." or "_" (the go tool's own rules); paths relative to root joined by "/", sorted (JavaScript's default sort). imports: for every file of files, the module's own packages it imports as directories, in first-seen order, each once: an import path equal to the module path → ".", starting with the module path + "/" → the rest; every other import is left out; with no module path every list is []. The paths are the quoted strings of the import declarations: a line starting with `import` followed by an optional name (an identifier, "." or "_") and a quoted path, and each line of an `import (` ... `)` block holding a quoted path once its `//` comment is removed. → {files, imports}.
